criteria.rationale: Examined D1, D2, gitCommandContext and the four converted readers against the cause (a stat-cache refresh changing .git). Optional locks off in the shared constructor plus git status instead of work-tree diff addresses that cause for R1, and the focused index tests pass. The design delta reports no structural deltas, so there is nothing to map. Answer drift is reported separately.

Searched POSE.md and the help catalog for report --since and validate --changed-from. They describe a Git ref and no index behaviour, so no operational document, template or scaffold needs a change. The inaccurate equivalence claim in the code comment and D1 is in N7.
Compared the pose-mcp diff of the two fix commits with the spec's artifacts and affected areas. The eight code files match, and no unrelated behaviour was added. artifact-check --strict exited 0.

Optional locks alone is the smallest change, and D1 records that git diff still rewrites the index with it, while a private index copy breaks the no-write dry run. A status-based helper of about 130 lines with no speculative extension is proportionate. The choice stops holding where it cannot reproduce git diff answers, which N1 to N5 show must be corrected.

findings.action: The commits-since-base diff omits --ignore-submodules=none, which the replaced command had. The caller's -c diff.ignoreSubmodules=none does not override submodule.<name>.ignore in .gitmodules, so with ignore=all a committed gitlink change is dropped. Reproduced: git diff with the old flags named .gitmodules and mod; WorktreeChangedNames named only .gitmodules. validate --changed-from (validate_scope.go:108) and report --since can then select or list less, against the rule that configuration never hides a changed gitlink.

For a path changed both in commits and in the work tree, a submodule is compared only by its checked-out HEAD. A submodule checked out at the base commit with uncommitted content is dropped. Reproduced: git diff <base> names mod, WorktreeChangedNames returns nothing, so scope selection narrows. L2 covers only mode changes and claims listing never reports less.

For paths changed in both places, hash-object follows symlinks and Lstat errors other than not-exist are fatal. Reproduced: a dangling symlink (also one restored to its base target) fails with exit 128, and a directory replaced by a file fails with ENOTDIR (line 118); git diff answered both. A link is compared by its target's content, not by its link text. validate --changed-from then fails with 'revision unknown?' and drops the cause (validate_scope.go:110), and report --since silently lists nothing.

Every status with X=A is mapped to A, including the unmerged AA and AU states. The ledger drops A (review_attempt_ledger.go:575). Reproduced with an add/add conflict on a review-attempts record: git diff HEAD says M, WorktreeChanges says A, and ReviewRunHistoryFindings no longer reports the immutable evidence change that the previous --diff-filter=MDT read reported.

git status and diff name paths from the repository top level, but worktreeMatchesCommit joins them to root. With a POSE root in a subdirectory, a file added since base and modified in the work tree looks absent at both ends and is dropped. Reproduced: git diff names proj/new, WorktreeChangedNames returns nothing, so validation can narrow.

An intent-to-add entry (porcelain ' A') falls to the default M while git diff HEAD says A. Reproduced: git add -N of a new review-attempts record yields a false 'immutable review evidence changed' finding.

Names do not equal git diff <base> as D1 and the doc comment state. A change staged and then reverted in the work tree is still listed (also reported as M to the ledger), and after git rm --cached with the file at base content the path git diff names is omitted.

A range given as base (A..B or A...) used to be accepted by git diff and now fails, because HEAD is appended as a further revision (exit 129). report --since then silently lists no files (report.go:298-301) and validate --changed-from A..B errors.

The R2 and R3 tests do not run ReviewRunHistoryFindings, one of the changed readers. The equivalence test in internal/pose has no case for conflicts, intent-to-add, staged-then-reverted, submodules, symlinks, a subdirectory root or a range base, so N1 to N8 pass it.
